subject: Urban Planning
title: Cabrini-Green: Chicago's Vertical Ghetto
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cabrini-Green: Chicago's Vertical Ghetto.

hook.text: Cabrini-Green had 15,000 residents in 23 high-rise towers on Chicago's Near North Side. It became a symbol of failure.

buildup.text: Built in the 1940s-60s, the project concentrated poverty in towers with broken elevators, no heat, and gang control.

discovery.text: The failure wasn't architecture. It was policy — no maintenance funding, no jobs program, no mixed income.

twist.text: When the towers were demolished, residents were promised replacement housing. Most never received it.

climax.text: Luxury condos and a Target now sit where Cabrini-Green stood. The land was valuable — the people weren't.

punchline.text: Tear down public housing. Build luxury condos. Call it progress.

quiz.question: What happened to Cabrini-Green residents after demolition?
options: They moved into new mixed-income developments on the same site
Most never received the replacement housing they were promised
They were relocated to newly renovated public housing nearby
